issues.description: Format B assumes metrics is a dict, so a structurally invalid metrics value raises AttributeError instead of producing a malformed_row warning.
Malformed Format C XML is not caught, so ET.ParseError crashes ingestion despite the parser contract saying warnings never raise.
NaN/Infinity scores are accepted and not validated as finite, which can violate the [0, 1] contract or crash SQLite writes.
Format B missing/null required fields are coerced to strings or empty values and ingested instead of being rejected as malformed rows.
Format C missing run_id/model/task values become empty canonical fields and can collapse unrelated bad records under the same key.
Duplicate correction semantics are applied to all sources, silently overwriting Format A/C duplicates even though only Format B documents correction behavior.
An empty input directory returns an error only after ingest creates a new SQLite schema file.
Reports omit sources with zero ingested rows, so an all-skipped or absent source is invisible except in the total.
The database schema does not enforce non-empty identifiers or score bounds, leaving canonical invariants entirely dependent on parser correctness.
All input files are read or parsed as whole documents, which is fragile for large evaluation outputs and avoidable for CSV/JSONL.
